solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skin of panther spotted, killed for food

indicators.note: the skin of something is its outside, so only the outer letters of the word panther are kept

parts.note: spotted means seen, eyed

explanation.surface: A panther's spotted coat, perhaps from an animal killed and eaten by another predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like it describes the panther's skin, but it means seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator that preyed on an animal hunted and killed it to eat.

clue.text: Upset, and not to perform musical piece

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: and not is NOR
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A nervous musician, distressed, refuses to play a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Treaty's set for continuous talks

indicators.note: set here means arranged or put in order, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A treaty is agreed as the outcome of ongoing negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continuous talks' reads as diplomatic negotiations but is a verb phrase: one who yatters talks without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To yatter is to chatter on and on, idle talk that never stops.

clue.text: Deserts peer, abandoning king

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the king's letter is dropped from the peer

parts.note: a duke is a peer of the realm
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman runs away and leaves his monarch behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a verb (runs away) but is the noun, as in getting one's just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: One's deserts are what one deserves, which is what is owed or one's rightful reward.

clue.text: Modern, heavyweight physicist

parts.note: modern means new
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A description of a present-day, highly influential scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Danger! Bus damaged car bumpers

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a bus has crashed into the bumpers of cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudge bars are metal guards fitted to the front of vehicles to protect against minor impacts.

clue.text: Fighting to get hold of iron that's very thin

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: fighting between nations is war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Combat to seize a very thin sheet of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a very thin slice or biscuit, hence the phrase wafer-thin.

clue.text: One for free initially being flogged at a reduced price?

indicators.note: being flogged means being beaten, so the letters are knocked into a new order
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word free is used

explanation.surface: A shop offering one item free, selling things off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' suggests sold, but it signals the anagram of ONEFORF.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on offer are on special sale, typically discounted; the question mark admits this is one example.

clue.text: Don't need to be arranged in a row

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone saying there is no need to set things out in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed end to end are lined up one after another in a line.

clue.text: Defensive blunder by father leaves one hopping!

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
OG is short for own goal, a defender's error in football

explanation.surface: A father's footballing error makes a player hop about in pain or fury.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal (OG) is when a defender accidentally scores against their own side in football.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an amphibian that moves by leaping, a typical hopping creature.

clue.text: Scent something sometimes blown in your face?

definitions.meaning: to scent is to smell out

definitions.text: something sometimes blown in your face?
definitions.meaning: in the middle of your face and gets blown

explanation.surface: A perfume that is sprayed into someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose is to detect by smell; a nose is the facial feature one blows into a handkerchief.

clue.text: Unusual for a clef to get lost

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A musical clef going missing would be out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rude ways to tell someone to go away.

clue.text: Tend to put in thick rope that can be washed

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope
to tend is to lean or incline towards

explanation.surface: An instruction to place some washable thick rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cleanable is able to be cleaned, such as washed.

clue.text: Decent time obtained in pursuit

indicators.note: obtained in means found within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit

explanation.surface: A reasonable time recorded in a race or hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, so morally decent.

clue.text: Own house containing opening for electric lift!

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the opening letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A homeowner's house has a gap where an electric lift will go.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave-ho is the call sailors gave while hauling together, a shout accompanying a heavy pull.

clue.text: Venomous types putting two and two together?

definitions.meaning: people or machines that add numbers

explanation.surface: Snakes who are good at working things out.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake; an adder is also one who adds up figures.

clue.text: Where some Cambridge students are drinking

explanation.surface: Students at Cambridge are known for their drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing College is one of Cambridge's colleges; downing pints is quaffing them.

clue.text: Birds and pigs messed with lawn

indicators.note: messed with means disturbed or jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Birds and pigs have churned up a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapwings are plovers with a crested head, common farmland birds.

clue.text: Abuse was rained on new girl at first

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so the initial letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A newly arrived girl is first showered with insults.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrong someone is to treat them unjustly, to mistreat them.

clue.text: Bait Mike put on end of line, twisting

indicators.note: put on the end of means placed after, so Mike comes last
twisting means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a line
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An angler called Mike fixes bait to the end of a twisting fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' suggests a fishing line, but it is a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Worms are the classic live bait put on a fishing hook.

clue.text: Girl got up around one

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: rose means got up
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl woke and got out of bed at about one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Rosie, a pet form of Rose or Rosemary, is a female first name.

clue.text: Building toy stage, round

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or contest
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A list of things: a construction toy, a theatre stage, a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the brand of interlocking plastic bricks children build with.

clue.text: Craziest club: try to get one admitted

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: to test is to try
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild nightclub tries to get someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty means crazy, so the battiest is the maddest of all.

clue.text: Little thanks given to daughter

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A daughter receives only a small amount of gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a small amount, a little bit.

clue.text: Language employed by Sheraton guest

indicators.note: employed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The language spoken by a guest staying at a Sheraton hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, as in mother tongue.

clue.text: Tenacious, if troubled

definitions.meaning: to be ... by something is to be plagued by it

explanation.surface: Someone persists even when they are worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged describes determined persistence; being dogged by bad luck means being continually beset by it.
